raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> **RFC / draft.** This proposes small platform seams so the plugin-kernel (megakernel) contract can be served by out-of-tree platforms. Feedback on the shape of the seams matters more than the code right now; the names are open.

## Motivation

The megakernel contract (`sglang.kernels.plugin_kernels.nvidia.spec` + `sglang.srt.kernel_plugins.nvidia.binding`) is mostly hardware-neutral: a registry of per-architecture specs, refused-by-default features, `BuildContext` / `Step` / `BuiltMegakernel`, an install point after model load and before KV sizing, and the `plan` / `forward` split. Only a few places tie it to CUDA:

1. The only flag is `--enable-nvidia-megakernel`.
2. Specs are matched on a `torch.cuda` ISA probe (`sm_XY`); with no CUDA device every spec is refused with "no GPU is visible".
3. Install calls `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` and reads the SM count unconditionally.
4. Dispatch is always a `model.forward` wrapper plus a CUDA-graph capture check. A platform whose graph runner never calls `model.forward` for decode (it runs precompiled graphs) has no place to hook in.
5. A megakernel can't ask for KV / state pools in its own layout, even though it is built before the KV cache is sized.

How we found this: we are bringing up a whole-model decode kernel on AWS Trainium (trn3) as an out-of-tree SGLang platform plugin (the plugin repo is private for now). To use the upstream contract we had to copy it into the plugin and monkeypatch around the five points above: an env var stood in for the flag, we wrapped the `handle_nvidia_megakernel` resolution step and the `install_megakernel` module name, the Neuron graph runner did the dispatch, and the platform's `get_kv_pool_cls` hook selected pools in the kernel's layout. Every one of those patches maps to one of the small seams below.

## Modifications

All changes are backward compatible. With no new flag set and an in-tree platform, behavior is unchanged.

- **`--enable-megakernel`** (new `exec` field, appended to `POSITIONAL_FIELD_ORDER`): the platform-agnostic flag. `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` still works and means the same thing: `flag_enabled()` accepts either one, in both resolution and `megakernel_enabled()`.
- **Device target through the platform:** new `SRTPlatform.get_megakernel_target() -> Optional[str]`. The default returns the same `sm_<major><minor>` that `device_isa()` computed before, for CUDA-alike platforms, and None otherwise. `binding.device_isa()` now delegates to it. `Requirements.isas` now documents that it holds these target strings (e.g. `"trn3"` out of tree).
- **Out-of-tree platforms skip CUDA-only checks:** the `sgl-nvidia-mega` entry-point check (an OOT platform registers specs from its own plugin; an empty registry is still reported by `find_spec`), `torch.cuda.mem_get_info` in the build log, and the SM-count residency check. An OOT spec that sets `resident_blocks` is refused with a message pointing to `model_disable_reasons`.
- **Optional decode-graph-backend requirement:** this already worked (an empty `Requirements.decode_graph_backends` accepts any backend). It is now documented for platforms whose own runner dispatches.
- **Platform-owned dispatch:** new `SRTPlatform.install_megakernel_dispatch(*, model, built, binding) -> bool`, called once after the build. Returning True means the platform's graph runner plans and runs covered steps (`built.plan` / `built.forward`), so core installs neither the `model.forward` wrapper nor the CUDA-graph capture check. The default False keeps today's wrapper.
- **Optional `pool_layout` on the built megakernel:** if `getattr(built, "pool_layout", None)` is not None, it goes to the new `SRTPlatform.activate_megakernel_pool_layout(pool_layout)` right after the build, which is before KV sizing. The platform's `get_kv_pool_cls` (and friends) can then build pools in that layout. The base implementation raises `NotImplementedError`, which becomes the binding's usual "cannot run this setup" refusal. In-tree pools have one layout each, so nothing in-tree accepts a layout yet.

Design rationale:
- **Platform hooks instead of a parallel `kernel_plugins/<vendor>` copy.** The contract and registry stay shared; the platform answers three questions: what the device target is, whether it owns dispatch, and whether it can build a given pool layout.
- **Extend the existing contract instead of forking it.** Field names stay the same, so specs written for NVIDIA keep working unchanged and an OOT spec reads the same.
- **Dispatch through the platform runner.** On platforms where decode never goes through `model.forward` (precompiled graphs), the graph runner is the only place a step is actually chosen.
- **`pool_layout` is optional and refused by default.** Only a platform that implements `activate_megakernel_pool_layout` can accept one. A kernel that declares a layout implicitly promises to cover every decode step, because the standard path cannot read those pools. This PR leaves that check to the platform. It could move into core, see open questions.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change on in-tree platforms: the default code paths are the same as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A (startup-only code paths).

## Tests

- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/kernel_plugins/nvidia/test_megakernel_platform_hooks.py` (registered `base-a` / cpu like its neighbors). It covers:
  - `--enable-megakernel` and `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` both enable the binding.
  - A spec matches on an OOT target and not on `sm_103`.
  - A platform that owns dispatch keeps `model.forward` and gets no capture hook; the default still wraps.
  - `pool_layout` reaches the platform; the `SRTPlatform` default refuses it.
- Run locally on macOS (CPU only): `test/registered/unit/kernel_plugins/nvidia/` (12 passed: 8 existing + 4 new), `test/registered/unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py` (passed), and `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py` (389 passed; 3 failures from `xgrammar` / `mlx` not being installed in the local venv, unrelated to this change).
- **Not tested:** any GPU run, an actual `sgl-nvidia-mega` spec, and the Trainium integration against this exact branch. The plugin's version of these seams runs as monkeypatches against an older main.

## Open questions

1. **Naming:** should `Requirements.isas` become `targets` (with `isas` as an alias)? Should the contract move out of the `nvidia` package (e.g. `plugin_kernels/spec.py`, re-exported from `nvidia`)? This PR keeps file locations to stay minimal.
2. **Messages and log lines** still say `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` / "NVIDIA megakernel". Should those strings come from the platform?
3. **AMD monokernel:** should `--enable-megakernel` also cover the AMD monokernel binding, or should the two contracts be unified first?
4. **`pool_layout` coverage:** should core enforce that a kernel declaring `pool_layout` covers every decode step (e.g. `plan` returning None becomes an error)?
5. **Draft models:** should a draft spec be allowed to declare a `pool_layout`? It is currently passed through like the target's.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""CPU checks of the platform seams of the megakernel binding: --enable-megakernel,
+the device target, a platform-owned dispatch and a built pool_layout."""
+
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.kernels.plugin_kernels.nvidia import spec as registry
+from sglang.srt.kernel_plugins.nvidia import binding
+from sglang.srt.platforms.interface import SRTPlatform
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import publish, reset_context
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
+from _fakes import ARCH, SPEC, FakeBuilt, Lm, batch, server_args  # noqa: E402
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, stage="base-a", runner_config="cpu")
+
+TARGET = "fake_accel_v1"
+
+
+class OotPlatform:
+    """An out-of-tree platform: no torch.cuda, its own target and graph runner."""
+
+    activate_megakernel_pool_layout = SRTPlatform.activate_megakernel_pool_layout
+
+    def __init__(self, *, owns_dispatch=False, accepts_layouts=False):
+        self.owns_dispatch, self.accepts_layouts = owns_dispatch, accepts_layouts
+        self.dispatched, self.layouts = [], []
+
+    def is_cuda_alike(self):
+        return False
+
+    def is_out_of_tree(self):
+        return True
+
+    def get_megakernel_target(self):
+        return TARGET
+
+    def install_megakernel_dispatch(self, *, model, built, binding):
+        self.dispatched.append(built)
+        return self.owns_dispatch
+
+    def accept(self, layout):
+        self.layouts.append(layout)
+
+
+class LayoutBuilt(FakeBuilt):
+    pool_layout = "kernel-native"
+
+
+SPEC_OOT = registry.MegakernelSpec(
+    name="fake-oot",
+    requires=registry.Requirements(
+        isas=frozenset({TARGET}),
+        tp_sizes=frozenset(),
+        decode_graph_backends=frozenset(),
+    ),
+    features=SPEC.features,
+    numerics=SPEC.numerics,
+    max_rows=8,
+    build=lambda model, hf, ctx: FakeBuilt(ctx.widths),
+    api_version=registry.MEGAKERNEL_API_VERSION,
+)
+SPEC_LAYOUT = registry.MegakernelSpec(
+    **{
+        **{f: getattr(SPEC_OOT, f) for f in SPEC_OOT.__struct_fields__},
+        "build": lambda model, hf, ctx: LayoutBuilt(ctx.widths),
+    }
+)
+
+
+def install(platform, *, hooks=None):
+    lm = Lm()
+    with (
+        patch.object(binding, "current_platform", platform),
+        patch.object(binding, "deadline_s", return_value=30.0),
+        patch.object(binding, "_gather_tp", side_effect=lambda x, group=None: [x]),
+        patch.object(binding, "_tokens_per_request", return_value=1),
+        patch.object(binding, "_decode_graphs_enabled", return_value=True),
+    ):
+        binding.install_megakernel(
+            model=lm,
+            hf_config=SimpleNamespace(architectures=[ARCH]),
+            capture_tail_hooks=[] if hooks is None else hooks,
+            is_draft=False,
+        )
+    return lm
+
+
+class TestMegakernelPlatformHooks(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        registry_patch = patch.dict(registry._REGISTRY, clear=True)
+        registry_patch.start()
+        self.addCleanup(registry_patch.stop)
+        self.addCleanup(reset_context)
+
+    def _publish(self, **flags):
+        publish(server_args(**flags), role="test")
+
+    def test_enable_megakernel_is_the_platform_agnostic_spelling(self):
+        self._publish()
+        self.assertFalse(binding.megakernel_enabled())
+        reset_context()
+        self._publish(enable_megakernel=True)
+        self.assertTrue(binding.megakernel_enabled())
+        reset_context()
+        self._publish(enable_nvidia_megakernel=True)
+        self.assertTrue(binding.megakernel_enabled())
+
+    def test_specs_match_the_platform_target(self):
+        registry.register(architecture=ARCH, path=f"{__name__}:SPEC_OOT")
+        with patch.object(binding, "current_platform", OotPlatform()):
+            self.assertEqual(binding.device_isa(), TARGET)
+        spec, why = registry.find_spec(architectures=[ARCH], isa=TARGET)
+        self.assertIs(spec, SPEC_OOT, why)
+        spec, why = registry.find_spec(architectures=[ARCH], isa="sm_103")
+        self.assertIsNone(spec)
+        self.assertIn("not sm_103", why)
+
+    def test_a_platform_that_owns_dispatch_keeps_the_model_forward(self):
+        registry.register(architecture=ARCH, path=f"{__name__}:SPEC_OOT")
+        self._publish(enable_megakernel=True)
+        platform, hooks = OotPlatform(owns_dispatch=True), []
+        lm = install(platform, hooks=hooks)
+        built = binding.built_megakernel(lm)
+        self.assertEqual(platform.dispatched, [built])
+        self.assertNotIn("forward", lm.__dict__)
+        self.assertEqual(hooks, [], "no CUDA-graph capture check")
+        self.assertEqual(lm(batch(2).input_ids, None, batch(2)), "standard")
+
+        # The default (False) keeps core's model.forward wrapper.
+        lm = install(OotPlatform(owns_dispatch=False))
+        self.assertIn("forward", lm.__dict__)
+
+    def test_a_pool_layout_goes_to_the_platform_before_dispatch(self):
+        registry.register(architecture=ARCH, path=f"{__name__}:SPEC_LAYOUT")
+        self._publish(enable_megakernel=True)
+        platform = OotPlatform(owns_dispatch=True)
+        platform.activate_megakernel_pool_layout = platform.accept
+        install(platform)
+        self.assertEqual(platform.layouts, ["kernel-native"])
+        # SRTPlatform's default refuses a layout its pools cannot build.
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "declares a pool_layout"):
+            install(OotPlatform(owns_dispatch=True))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
